To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
estrogen receptor immunoreactive levels are altered in behavior-relevant brain regions during pregnancy.
the expression of ER-ir is altered in the MPN and the VMN during the course of pregnancy and postpartum day one.
the levels of ER protein are altered in behavior-relevant brain regions at critical times during pregnancy and parturition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how estrogen affects the brain and behavior during pregnancy and at parturition.
how estrogen acts within specific regions of the brain to regulate maternal behavior.
the neuroendocrine control of female reproduction.

ER protein levels are differentially regulated during pregnancy and postpartum, and these changes may underlie the dramatic changes in maternal and sexual behaviors that occur around the time of birth.
the levels of estrogen receptors in the medial preoptic area and ventromedial hypothalamus change during pregnancy and that these changes are regionally and temporaly specific.
the levels of ER protein within the MPN and the VMN are regulated in a regionally- and temporally-specific manner during pregnancy and parturition.

the sensitivity of the medial preoptic and ventromedial nuclei to estrogen is increased during pregnancy.
estrogen receptor levels are altered in brain regions that regulate maternal and sexual behavior during pregnancy.
ER-ir is increased in the MPN and the VMN on days 16 and 22 of pregnancy and on postpartum (PPT) day 1, but not in the medial amydgala.

estrogen receptors are regulated in a temporally and spatially specific manner during pregnancy and parturition.
